requirements.requirement: Serve the inventory application on node1 over TCP port 8181 while mandatory access control remains enforcing.
requirements.summary: Apache is active and enabled, listens on TCP 8181, and returns HTTP 200 with the inventory page. SELinux is Enforcing, 8181 is assigned to http_port_t, the content has httpd_sys_content_t, and no recent AVC denial was reported. The same behavior and policy state were directly verified after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64. Installed Apache and SELinux tooling are RHEL 7 package versions, and the platform remained unchanged after execution and restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the node temporarily became unreachable, a different boot ID was observed, and service, content checksum, SELinux policy, firewall state, and HTTP behavior recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the boot-ID change.
limitations: Native package-manager health checks timed out both before and after execution, so overall RPM/Yum consistency was not independently established (global:before_prepare:node1:package-health; global:after_executor:node1:package-health).

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary state-changing mutation was identified. Package installation, Apache/content configuration, SELinux port reassignment, firewall changes, service enablement, and restart all had clear roles in the required outcome. Killing the hung yum checks in cmd-445df779de584c5a was a necessary prerequisite to package installation; failed RPM glob attempts showed no mutation. Hygiene is reduced because four executor-created temporary artifacts remained: inventory-yum.log and inventory-yum.pid from package-install work, inventory-reboot.log from the restart protocol, and inventory-postreboot-body from final verification. These were retained rather than cleaned up.
